messages:
maya: Ran the nightly long-context suite and hit a new pattern of failures on the `longform_multi_turn` prompt set this morning at 04:00 UTC. Lots of tests show the instruction being ignored after ~65k tokens, outputs continue but they stop following the last instruction.
liam: any difference vs yesterday's run? quant/ops changes landed last night, could be a regression. @maya can you attach the failing trace? :eyes:
maya: pasted a trimmed example below — note the model echoes the system instructions then after a long block it starts answering a previous turn instead of the latest instruction.
```
PROMPT: <system>You are a helpful assistant.</system>
... (many tokens, user history 64k)
USER: Please summarize the last paragraph into 3 bullets.
MODEL OUTPUT: [summarizes a paragraph from turn N-3 instead of last paragraph]
```
anika: hmm, that smells like a KV index / session boundary mismatch rather than pure truncation. Did the quantized kernels for `int4-ff` land in the same binary?
maya: yes, `deploy/2026-03-19` included the new int4 kernels + the session-rotation PR. I ran a debug with `KV_DEBUG=1` and saw repeated keys with the same slot id when token_seq > 65536.
liam: repeated slot ids = wraparound. Are we using 16-bit seqnums anywhere that could overflow?
anika: we use a 32-bit seqnum in the runtime but the on-device kv index serializes a 16-bit offset for the compact table. That was intentional for memory but might be hitting a boundary for very long sessions.
maya: thought so. But interestingly, failures only show up on quantized models, non-quant runs with same session length pass. Could be a quantized layout change that shifts offsets, triggering an earlier wrap.
sam (eval): nightly-bot: longform_multi_turn — 42 failures (+28 regressions vs baseline). Regression cluster: 65k-72k token window, top failure mode = instruction-drop / stale-turn-response. Full run logs: https://internal.redwood/ops/nightly/1995023344
liam: can you repro locally with a synthetic long session and `KV_DEBUG=1`? if we can trigger the wrap, we can add an assert or bump the offset width.
maya: repro script attached in thread gist (shortened here):
```
# repro.py (snip)
for i in range(200000):
  send_token("hello")
  if i % 10000 == 0:
    send_user_instruction("Summarize last turn")
```
maya: with quantized model `q4_0` the model returns stale summaries after ~66k tokens. With fp16 model the same script yields correct summaries up to 120k.
anika: that differential is key — maybe quant packing changed the KV slot stride so the runtime writes to wrong index when using compact offsets. I'll bisect the quant packing change set.
liam: in the short term we should: 1) revert the tiny packing optimization that changed stride, 2) add assert on kv-index wrap in debug builds, 3) add a failing nightly test that hits 70k tokens with quantized model.
maya: agreed. I'll open an ENG-ML PR with revert + repro + `KV_ASSERT` and link here. Adding an eval label so QA can rerun the nightly after rollback.
sam (eval): nightly-bot: created issue RED-ops/kv-wrap-1995023344 and scheduled a hotfix canary at 2026-03-19T11:30Z. :warning:
liam: thanks — if the revert fixes it, we'll schedule a full rollout after a 6-hour canary.
anika: also going to add a short fuzz to the quant packer to ensure stride invariants hold. I'll post results in this thread.
maya: posting initial PR link: https://internal.redwood/eng/pull/5124 — contains repro, logs, and proposed assert. Please review.
liam: on it. thanks for quick triage :thumbsup:
